column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the victory “salvation” and says the people heard, rather than that they were told.
The Hebrew repeats stealing into the city; BSB first describes returning quietly.
The Hebrew repeats the king as the one crying; BSB leaves the second subject implicit.
The Hebrew locates the servants’ disgrace in their “faces” and repeatedly calls the saved life “soul”; BSB leaves the faces implicit and uses life language.
The Hebrew says it would be right “in your eyes”; BSB has “it would have pleased you”.
The Hebrew describes comforting speech as speaking to the servants’ heart; BSB says “speak comfort”.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats all the people as coming and calls each man’s destination his “tents”, plural; BSB uses “they all” and “home”.
The Hebrew names the palm of the enemies and the palm of the Philistines; BSB uses “hand” for both.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “his house” for both the return destination and the place where the report reached him; BSB varies “his palace” and “his quarters”.
The Hebrew says “my bone and my flesh”; BSB has “my own flesh and blood”.
The Hebrew repeats “my bone and my flesh” and says he will serve “before me all the days”; BSB has “flesh and blood” and “from this time”.
The Hebrew uses singular “heart” of all the men; BSB has plural “hearts”.
The Hebrew twice names the king as the one met and escorted; BSB uses pronouns.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they crossed the Jordan; BSB says they rushed down to it.

The Hebrew uses singular “adversary” for the sons of Zeruiah; BSB has plural “adversaries”.

The Hebrew calls Mephibosheth “Saul’s son”; BSB specifies “Saul’s grandson”.
The Hebrew says he came to Jerusalem; BSB has “from Jerusalem”.
The Hebrew leaves the deceiving servant unnamed, places the deception before the quoted plan, and says “I will saddle”; BSB names Ziba, puts the deception last, and has “have my donkey saddled”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “my father’s house” and calls them “men of death”; BSB has “my grandfather” and “deserves death”.
The Hebrew says “I have said”; BSB has “I hereby declare”.
The Hebrew leaves the recipient of everything unnamed; BSB supplies Ziba.
